It is argued, that the allegation against the petitioner is that he used to fill-out certain online forms using the digital signatures of one Anil Nanda; and used to perform the requisite steps to transfer the shareholding of Anil Nada in M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt. 7. Mr. Hossain however points-out, that other than the bald allegation that the petitioner helped the principal accused Awaneesh Chandra Jha in transferring the shareholding of M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt. Ltd. in the latter's favour, no material has come on record to substantiate that allegation.

9.

Mr. Hossain also points-out, that it is relevant to note that the petitioner has not been party to any civil dispute or settlement between the concerned parties, which only goes to show that apart from his professional engagement, the petitioner had not connection what was being done by Awaneesh Chandra Jha in relation to M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt. Ltd. or any other asset or property belonging to the complainant.

10. Moreover, it is pointed-out, that a perusal of the balance-sheet of M/s.
Saraltech Creations Pvt. Ltd. for the relevant years, would show that the said company had no fixed assets in its name at all, meaning thereby there was no property in Shimla belonging to the company that could have got transferred in favour of Awaneesh Chandra Jha by transferring the shareholding of the company.
In this behalf, attention is drawn to the independent auditor's reports and certain balance sheets relating to M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt. Ltd., copies of which have been placed on record.

sentences.text: Furthermore, Mr. Hossain has drawn attention to order dated 10.01.2025 made by this Bench in BAIL APPLN. No. 4120/2023, whereby this court has granted regular bail to the petitioner on very similar allegations, viz. the allegation that the petitioner had assisted in changing the shareholding pattern and directorship of another company in favour of Awaneesh Chandra Jha.

13. In the present case, it is argued that the petitioner has been in judicial custody ever-since the time of his arrest on 29.04.2023; investigation in the matter is complete; chargesheet dated 19.07.2023 has been filed in the matter; but trial is yet to commence, with 20 witnesses having been cited on behalf of the prosecution.
14.
Accordingly, in the meantime the petitioner has suffered custody of more than 01 year and 09 months; and it is clear that trial in the matter will take significant time to conclude.

15. Opposing the grant of bail, Mr. Tarang Srivastava, learned APP appearing on behalf of the State has argued that the petitioner's role in the matter is central, inasmuch as without his connivance and expertise in transferring the shareholding of M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt. Ltd. in favour of Awaneesh Chandra Jha, the latter could not have achieved the purpose of transferring the Shimla property to his benefit.
16. Learned APP argues, that in consideration of the job performed for Awaneesh Chandra Jha, the petitioner has received a 'handsome amount'.

17. Mr. Srivastva submits, that evidence incriminating the petitioner, by way of WhatsApp chats,
electronic evidence relating to the video- verification link for transferring shareholding on the MCA portal, along with forged PAN cards and Aadhar cards have also come on record in the course of the investigation.

18. Learned APP has stressed that WhatsApp chats, which corroborate that the petitioner was executing various acts at the instance of Awaneesh Chandra Jha, have been recovered from their mobile phones, which chats are pending examination by the FSL.

19. However, upon being queried, Mr. Srivastva fairly submits, that the aforementioned evidence has come on record in a different FIR i.e., FIR No. 295/2022 dated 24.12.2022 registered at P.S.:
Crime Branch, Delhi and not in the present FIR bearing No. 97/2022.

Mr. Srivastva clarifies, that once the FSL report in respect of the said WhatsApp chats and other electronic evidence is received,
they would file a supplementary chargesheet in the present case to show the petitioner's role.

It is accordingly argued that further incriminating material against the petitioner is yet to come on record.

23. Upon a conspectus of the facts and circumstances obtaining in the matter, the considerations what weigh with the court at this stage are the following :
23.1.

The allegations levelled against the petitioner in the chargesheet evidently proceed on the disclosure statements alleged to have been made by the petitioner and other co-accused persons; no cogent material or evidence appears to have come on record to substantiate those allegations; and no recovery appears to have been made from the petitioner;

23.2. As presently drawn-up, the chargesheet ascribes to the petitioner only the role of having aided the principal accused Awaneesh Chandra Jha in gaining control of M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt.
Ltd., by having the shareholding of that company transferred to himself, which transfer is alleged to have resulted in the transfer of ownership of the Shimla property to Awaneesh Chandra Jha.

However, the audited balance sheets of the company do not show the Shimla property as a fixed asset standing in the name of M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt. Ltd.; and in fact, M/s. Saraltech Creations Pvt. Ltd. appears to have no fixed asset going by those audited balance sheets; 23.4.

In the circumstances, this court is persuaded to allow the present petition and to admit the petitioner - Mazid Ali s/o Sajid Ali - to regular bail pending trial subject to the following conditions :
24.1.

The petitioner shall furnish a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rs.
Fifty Thousand Only) with 02 sureties in the like amount from relatives, to the satisfaction of the learned trial court.

As requested, the petitioner is permitted to furnish sureties at the hands of the same relatives, who may furnished sureties for him in compliance of order dated 10.01.2025 passed by this court in BAIL APPLN.

The petitioner shall furnish to the Investigating Officer, a cellphone number on which the petitioner may be contacted at any time and shall ensure that the number is kept active and switched-on at all times;
24.3. If the petitioner has a passport, he shall surrender the same to the learned trial court and shall not travel out of the country without prior permission of the learned trial court; 24.4.

The petitioner shall not contact, nor visit, nor offer any inducement,
threat or promise to any of the prosecution witnesses or other persons acquainted with the facts of case.
The petitioner shall not tamper with evidence nor otherwise The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

25. Since the petitioner is facing trial and is therefore appearing before the learned trial court from time-to-time, it is not considered necessary to impose a reporting requirement as a condition of regular bail.
